name: Berberine
short: No serious adverse reactions in a meta-analysis of 27 trials. A review advises caution in pregnancy, newborns and G6PD deficiency, and with medicines metabolised by CYP enzymes.
text: In a meta-analysis of 27 randomised trials (2569 patients), no serious adverse reaction was reported, although the overall quality of the included studies was limited. A toxicology review of barberry and berberine reported dose-dependent effects including gastrointestinal upset and jaundice, and advised caution in pregnancy, in newborns and in people with G6PD deficiency, and when berberine is taken with medicines metabolised by CYP enzymes, which it inhibits. In one of two dosing studies in healthy volunteers, berberine increased blood exposure to the medicine ciclosporin by about 19%, which the authors thought might partly reflect inhibition of CYP3A4.
